hooks.text: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their own bodies to survive.
Female anglerfish can grow up to sixty times larger than males.
A tiny male anglerfish permanently fuses into the body of a female.

title: The Deep Sea Fish Where Males Fuse Into Females
description: Discover how tiny male deep-sea anglerfish permanently fuse into massive females, dissolving their own organs to share a single bloodstream.

beats.text: Male deep-sea anglerfish dissolve their bodies to survive.
beats.visual: Deep-sea anglerfish female with attached male, Ceratias holboelli, ocean depths
queries: Deep sea anglerfish male and female

beats.text: Starting with the scale of everyday fish, researchers found there are more than two hundred species of anglerfish.
beats.visual: NOAA ROV exploration in the deep ocean, Deep Discoverer ROV

beats.text: Moving up the ladder, females use a bioluminescent lure on their heads to attract unsuspecting prey.
beats.visual: Bioluminescent esca and illicium of an anglerfish, Melanocetus johnsonii

beats.text: These massive females can stretch their jaws and stomachs to swallow prey up to twice their own size.
beats.visual: Black seadevil anglerfish in natural deep sea habitat

beats.text: At the extreme end of the scale, female deep-sea anglerfish can grow up to sixty times the size of the tiny males.
beats.visual: Scientific illustration of deep-sea anglerfish anatomy, Ceratiidae illustration

beats.text: When a male finally encounters a female, he latches onto her using his teeth.
beats.visual: Photocorynus spiniceps with attached male parasite

beats.text: Over time, the attached male physically fuses with the female, merging their blood vessels and skin.
beats.visual: Detailed specimen drawing of Ceratiidae with male parasite
